    {# =========================================================================
   templates/account.html.twig - "Manage my account" (USER role).
   Two independent forms on the same page:
     1. the modification (identity, login, optional new password), with
        the MyAccountType form;
     2. the deletion of the account - which also cancels its appointments: a
        hand-written form.
   Both require the CURRENT password (current_password field).
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends 'layout.html.twig' %}
{% import 'macros.html.twig' as m %}

{% block content %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">

    {# 1. modification #}
    <div class="card p-4 mb-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{{ 'MY_ACCOUNT.TITLE'|trans }}</h5>

      {{ form_start(form) }}
        {{ form_errors(form) }}
        {{ m.identity(form, invalidFields) }}

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">{{ 'PERSONS.ACCOUNT_SECTION'|trans }}</h6>
        {{ m.field(form.login, invalidFields) }}
        <div class="row g-3">
          <div class="col-sm-6">{{ m.field(form.password.first) }}</div>
          <div class="col-sm-6">{{ m.field(form.password.second) }}</div>
        </div>
        {{ m.field(form.current_password) }}

        <div class="d-flex gap-2 mt-4">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{{ 'PERSONS.SAVE'|trans }}</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{{ path('area') }}">{{ 'MY_ACCOUNT.BACK'|trans }}</a>
        </div>
      {{ form_end(form) }}
    </div>

    {# 2. deletion. The password field has the same NAME as that of the first
       form (current_password), but another id: two elements of the same
       page cannot have the same id #}
    <div class="card p-4 border-danger">
      <h5 class="card-title text-danger mb-1">{{ 'MY_ACCOUNT.DELETE_TITLE'|trans }}</h5>
      <p class="text-muted small">{{ 'MY_ACCOUNT.DELETE_HELP'|trans }}</p>
      <form method="post" action="{{ path('account_delete') }}" class="d-flex flex-wrap gap-2 align-items-end"
            data-confirmation="{{ 'MY_ACCOUNT.DELETE_CONFIRM'|trans }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="_token" value="{{ csrf_token('rdvmedecins') }}">
        <div class="flex-grow-1">
          <label class="form-label" for="delete_password">{{ 'MY_ACCOUNT.CURRENT_PASSWORD_LABEL'|trans }}</label>
          <input id="delete_password" name="current_password" type="password" maxlength="72"
                 autocomplete="current-password" required class="form-control">
        </div>
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-danger">{{ 'MY_ACCOUNT.DELETE_SUBMIT'|trans }}</button>
      </form>
    </div>

  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

    “Manage my account”: two independent forms on the same page.

    • Lines 18–38: the update, using the [MyAccountType] form: the identity fields, the login, the new password and its confirmation (optional), and the current password (required). The version (optimistic lock) is set by [form_end];
    • Lines 43–56: Account deletion, a handwritten form with its own current password field and a confirmation field. The field is named [current_password] (the field in the first form is named [my_account[current_password]]: the Form component prefixes its field names with the form name), and its own unique ID: two elements on a page cannot have the same ID, as indicated by the [for] attribute of a label.

{% block content %}

    /* =========================================================================
   public/css/styles.css - a few settings on top of Bootstrap
   (the same as in the other versions of this application).
   ========================================================================= */

body {
  background-color: #f5f7fa;
}

.free-slot:hover {
  background-color: #e9f7ef;
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   .error-zone: the error messages, at the bottom of the page, on a light pink background
   (see templates/fragments/errors.html.twig).
   position: sticky + bottom: if the page is taller than the window (a
   schedule of 12 slots, for example), the zone stays stuck to the bottom of the
   window instead of disappearing below the fold - without ever
   covering the content when the page is short.
   z-index: above the grey background of the booking dialog (.modal-backdrop).
   ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
.error-zone {
  position: sticky;
  bottom: 1rem;
  z-index: 1060;
  margin-top: 1.5rem;
  padding: 0.75rem 1rem;
  background-color: #fdecef; /* light pink */
  border: 1px solid #f5c2c7;
  border-radius: 0.375rem;
  color: #842029;
}

/* the two big options of the patient's "My area" page */
.option-card {
  transition: border-color 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s;
}

.option-card:hover {
  border-color: #0d6efd;

    // =========================================================================
// public/js/app.js - the ONLY JavaScript of the application.
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The whole application works without JavaScript. This script adds a
// convenience: before sending a form that carries the attribute
// data-confirmation="...", a modal dialog asks "Are you sure?"
// (the dialog itself is in the page: templates/fragments/confirmation.html.twig).
// If JavaScript is disabled, the form is simply sent without
// confirmation - nothing breaks ("progressive enhancement" principle).
//
// Why not window.confirm()? Its box cannot be styled, and its
// buttons stay in the language of the browser, not in that of the page.
// =========================================================================

(() => {
  const modal = document.getElementById('confirmation-modal');
  if (!modal) {
    return;
  }
  const message = document.getElementById('confirmation-modal-message');
  const noButton = modal.querySelector('.modal-footer [data-action="no"]');

  let pendingForm = null; // the form to send if the user confirms
  let previousFocus = null; // the element to give the focus back to on closing

  function open(form) {
    pendingForm = form;
    previousFocus = document.activeElement;
    // textContent (and not innerHTML): the message is displayed as TEXT,
    // never interpreted as HTML
    message.textContent = form.dataset.confirmation;
    modal.classList.remove('d-none');
    // the focus goes on "No": an absent-minded press on Enter deletes nothing
    noButton.focus();
  }

  function close() {
    modal.classList.add('d-none');
    pendingForm = null;
    if (previousFocus) {
      previousFocus.focus();
    }
  }

  // 1. we intercept the sending of the forms to confirm
  document.querySelectorAll('form[data-confirmation]').forEach((form) => {
    form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
      event.preventDefault();
      open(form);
    });
  });

  // 2. the buttons of the dialog (Yes / No / close cross)
  modal.addEventListener('click', (event) => {
    const action = event.target.closest('[data-action]')?.dataset.action;
    if (action === 'yes') {
      const form = pendingForm;
      close();
      // form.submit() sends the form WITHOUT triggering the
      // 'submit' event again: no new confirmation request
      form.submit();
    } else if (action === 'no') {
      close();
    } else if (event.target.classList.contains('modal')) {
      close(); // click on the grey background, outside the dialog
    }
  });

  // 3. keyboard: Escape closes the dialog; Tab stays INSIDE the dialog
  //    (otherwise the focus would go to the greyed-out page, behind)
  modal.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
    if (event.key === 'Escape') {
      close();
    } else if (event.key === 'Tab') {
      const buttons = [...modal.querySelectorAll('button')];
      const first = buttons[0];
      const last = buttons[buttons.length - 1];
      if (event.shiftKey && document.activeElement === first) {
        event.preventDefault();
        last.focus();
      } else if (!event.shiftKey && document.activeElement === last) {
        event.preventDefault();
        first.focus();
      }
    }
  });
})();

    The only [JavaScript] in the application—the one from Example 21—with a few additions. The entire application works without [JavaScript]: this script adds convenience by providing a confirmation before submitting a form that carries the [data-confirmation] attribute. If [JavaScript] is disabled, the form submits without confirmation: nothing breaks (principle of progressive enhancement).

    • Lines 15–19: The script is a function called as soon as it is defined ([(() => { ... })()]); its variables are not visible to the rest of the page. Without a confirmation window on the page, it does nothing;
    • Lines 26–35: Opening the window: the form to be submitted if the user confirms is stored, and the form’s message is displayed in the window. [textContent], not [innerHTML]: the message is displayed as text and is never interpreted as HTML. Focus moves to the “No” button: accidentally pressing Enter does not delete anything;
    • lines 37–43: closing the window; focus returns to the element that had it previously;
    • lines 46–51: the submission of each form to be confirmed is intercepted ([preventDefault] prevents it), and the window opens;
    • lines 54–67: the window’s buttons. A single handler for the entire window: [closest('[data-action]')] finds the clicked button or the element containing it. “Yes” submits the form via [form.submit()], which does not trigger the [submit] event: no new confirmation request is issued. Clicking on the grayed-out background outside the window closes it;
    • lines 71–86: the keyboard. Esc closes the window; the Tab key moves focus from one button to another without leaving the window (otherwise, it would move to the grayed-out page behind it): this is what users who navigate with the keyboard and screen readers expect.
